title: We directed UE 5.9's MCP AI Assistant (Gemini 4 Neon) to build a 4-tier, 343-prop Chaos Destruction system—zero hand-fractured meshes, 7 passes, ~$1.33 on subscription
author: Evening-Crab4100
selftext:
We wanted to see how far Unreal Engine 5.9's built-in MCP AI Assistant could go on a real gameplay system in our Action RPG (The Cindermarch), rather than a toy single-mesh demo. Over 7 directed passes (38 prompts with Gemini 4 Neon), we took a 343-prop bandit camp (176 instanced, 167 standalone) from static concrete to a 4-tier Chaos Destruction system without manually fracturing a mesh.

How it's structured:
- Zero idle physics cost: every prop stays a plain static/instanced mesh until struck, then swaps lazily into a Geometry Collection.
- 4 material/weight tiers: Tier 1 brittle clutter (bottles/mugs/jars), Tier 2 light wood (barrels splitting into staves + loose iron hoops, crates into planks), Tier 3 staged heavy furniture/wagons (tabletop cascade + rolling wheels), Tier 4 palisades and gates requiring heavier abilities to breach.

The 4 things that actually made it look right (and saved hours):
1. Hollow containers before fracturing (Pass 1 gave us solid pie-wedge barrels and cube crates).
2. Split wood along the grain instead of uniform Voronoi chunks.
3. Separate multi-part props first and anchor structural wall stumps into the ground so beams don't float mid-air.
4. Cap rubble counts, dust opacity, and audio duration (Pass 2 dust blinded the camera and smashing barrels accidentally leveled our sword proficiency).

Cost & caveats:
- 38 prompts came to roughly $1.33 of weekly allowance on a subscription plan.
- It still has minor rough edges we're planning to hand-polish, and one skill we started under the working name "Telekinesis" evolved into an orbiting stone ward that shreds props on sprint and fires in a volley.

Full breakdown video (4:48): https://youtu.be/XVtHVCv6cC0
Happy to answer questions on the Dataflow/Chaos setup or the Pass 1–7 prompts.
